lanes.label: Elsewhere in scripture
lanes.range: Topics in other books wired to this one

nodes.d: Exodus tells of Israel enslaved in Egypt (1:1-14) and delivered through the plagues, Passover and the sea (chapters 7-15), then of the covenant at Sinai (19-24) and the tabernacle (25-40), ending with the glory of the LORD filling it (40:34-38).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline Exodus in order, from the bondage in Egypt to the glory filling the tabernacle?
ev: Name the main sections: bondage, deliverance, the journey to Sinai, the law and covenant, and the tabernacle
Say where Exodus begins (1:1) and ends (40:38)

nodes.d: Jacob's family grows into a numerous people in Egypt, and a new king who did not know Joseph sets taskmasters over them and makes their lives bitter with hard bondage. The more they are afflicted, the more they multiply.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Israel went from being Joseph's family in Egypt to being slaves, and what happened the more they were afflicted?
ev: Say why the new king feared the Israelites (1:9-10)
Describe the work they were forced to do (1:11-14)

nodes.d: Pharaoh orders the Hebrew midwives to kill the baby boys, but Shiphrah and Puah fear God and let them live. God deals well with them, and Pharaoh then commands that every newborn son be cast into the river.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Shiphrah and Puah did when the king gave his order, and why?
ev: Name the two midwives (1:15)
Say what they did and why (1:17)
Say what Pharaoh then commanded all his people (1:22)

nodes.t: Moses is born and drawn from the water
nodes.d: A Levite woman hides her baby son for three months, then places him in a basket of bulrushes by the river. Pharaoh's daughter finds him, has compassion, and the baby's own mother is paid to nurse him; he is named Moses.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell how baby Moses was saved from the river?
ev: Retell how the baby was hidden and found (2:2-6)
Say who nursed him and why that was surprising (2:7-9)
Explain the meaning of the name Moses given in 2:10

nodes.t: Moses flees to Midian and God hears Israel's cry
nodes.d: Grown up, Moses kills an Egyptian who was beating a Hebrew, learns the deed is known, and flees to Midian, where he helps the priest's daughters and marries Zipporah. In Egypt the people groan, and God hears and remembers his covenant with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Moses ended up in Midian, and what 2:23-25 says God did about Israel's cry?
ev: Say why Moses left Egypt (2:11-15)
Say what Moses did at the well in Midian (2:16-17)
Find the verse that says God remembered his covenant (2:24)

nodes.d: While keeping Jethro's flock at Horeb, Moses sees a bush burning without being consumed. God calls him by name from it, declares the ground holy, identifies himself as the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, and says he has seen Israel's affliction and will send Moses to Pharaoh.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened at the burning bush and what God said to Moses there?
ev: Describe what Moses saw and what God told him to do with his shoes (3:2-5)
Say what God said he had seen and heard (3:7-9)
Say what God sent Moses to do (3:10)

nodes.t: "I AM": God's name and Moses' commission
nodes.d: Moses asks who he is to go to Pharaoh and what to tell Israel God's name. God promises to be with him, gives the name I AM THAT I AM and the LORD God of your fathers, and tells him what will happen: Pharaoh will refuse until God stretches out his hand.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what name God gave Moses to tell Israel, and what God promised him?
ev: Quote the name God gave in 3:14 from the Bible
Say the promise God gave Moses in 3:12
Say what God predicted about Pharaoh (3:19-20)

nodes.t: Three signs and Aaron as spokesman
nodes.d: Moses fears the people will not believe him. God gives him three signs (the rod that becomes a serpent, the leprous hand, water turned to blood). When Moses says he is slow of speech, God answers that he made man's mouth, is angry at the further refusal, and appoints Aaron as spokesman.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name the signs God gave Moses and say how God answered Moses' excuse about his speech?
ev: List the three signs (4:2-9)
Say how God answered Moses' complaint about his speech (4:11-12)
Say who God appointed to speak for Moses (4:14-16)

nodes.d: Moses leaves Jethro with his wife and sons, is told Israel is God's firstborn son and that Pharaoh's firstborn will die if he refuses, and is met by the LORD on the way, when Zipporah circumcises her son. Aaron meets him, and the elders believe and worship when they hear that God has visited them.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what God told Moses to say to Pharaoh in 4:22-23 and how the Israelites responded in 4:31?
ev: Say what message about "my son, even my firstborn" Moses was to give (4:22-23)
Say how the people responded (4:31)

nodes.d: The text says both that Pharaoh hardened his own heart and that the LORD hardened it, and ties this to the LORD multiplying his signs and being known and honoured. The topic invites careful reading of each verse without going beyond what is said.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} point to verses that say Pharaoh hardened his heart and verses that say the LORD hardened it, and say what purposes the text gives?
ev: Find one verse where Pharaoh hardens his own heart (8:15) and one where the LORD does (9:12)
Say what purposes God gives for the hardening (7:3-5, 9:16, 10:1-2, 14:4)

nodes.t: Pharaoh refuses and the work grows harder
nodes.d: Moses and Aaron ask Pharaoh to let Israel hold a feast to the LORD; he says he does not know the LORD and orders the people to make the same number of bricks while gathering their own straw. The officers blame Moses and Aaron, and Moses asks the LORD why he has not delivered his people.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what happened when Moses and Aaron first spoke to Pharaoh?
ev: Quote Pharaoh's answer in 5:2 in your own words
Say how the work changed (5:6-9)
Say what Moses asked God (5:22-23)

nodes.t: "I am the LORD": God's promises to redeem
nodes.d: God answers Moses by saying he is the LORD and has remembered his covenant with the patriarchs, then makes a series of promises: to bring Israel out, rid them of bondage, redeem them with a stretched out arm, take them as his people and be their God, and bring them to the land.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list what God promised Israel in 6:6-8 and say what he said he remembered?
ev: Name some of the promises God made to Israel in 6:6-8
Say what God said he had remembered (6:4-5)
Say how the people responded (6:9)

nodes.t: Redemption: the LORD brings his people out
nodes.d: Exodus uses redemption language: the LORD says he will redeem Israel with a stretched out arm (6:6), the song says the people he has led out are redeemed and purchased (15:13, 15:16), and the firstborn are redeemed (13:13-15). The topic traces this language.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} find where Exodus uses the word redeem and say what the LORD redeemed Israel from?
ev: Find a verse where God says he will redeem (6:6) and one in the song of the sea (15:13)
Say what the firstborn redemption in 13:13-15 recalls

nodes.t: The heads of the fathers' houses
nodes.d: A genealogy lists the sons of Reuben, Simeon and Levi, tracing Aaron and Moses to the house of Levi, then returns to the LORD's command to speak to Pharaoh, to which Moses answers that he is of uncircumcised lips.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say from which tribe Moses and Aaron came, according to this genealogy?
ev: Say which tribe Moses and Aaron came from (6:16-20)
Say what concern Moses repeated in 6:30

nodes.d: God says he has made Moses as a god to Pharaoh with Aaron as prophet, and that he will harden Pharaoh's heart. Aaron's rod becomes a serpent; the magicians do likewise, but Aaron's rod swallows theirs, and Pharaoh's heart stays hard.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened when Aaron cast down his rod before Pharaoh?
ev: Say what happened to Aaron's rod and the magicians' rods (7:10-12)
Say how Pharaoh responded (7:13)

nodes.t: The first plague: the river turned to blood
nodes.d: At the river's brink Moses and Aaron strike the water at the LORD's command; the river turns to blood, the fish die and the Egyptians cannot drink. The magicians do the same and Pharaoh's heart remains hard.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the first plague and how Pharaoh responded?
ev: Say what God said Pharaoh would know by this sign (7:17)
Say what happened to the river and the fish (7:20-21)

nodes.d: Frogs come up over Egypt into houses, beds and ovens. Pharaoh asks Moses to entreat the LORD and promises to let the people go; the frogs die at Moses' prayer, but when Pharaoh sees respite he hardens his heart.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Pharaoh promised during the plague of frogs and what he did afterwards?
ev: Say what Pharaoh promised and what he did when the frogs were gone (8:8, 8:15)

nodes.t: Lice and flies: a division between Israel and Egypt
nodes.d: Aaron strikes the dust and it becomes lice; the magicians cannot imitate it and say it is the finger of God. Swarms of flies then fill Egypt but not Goshen, where Israel lives, and Pharaoh offers a compromise before hardening his heart again.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what was different about the land of Goshen in the plague of flies?
ev: Say what the magicians said about the lice (8:19)
Say how Goshen was treated differently (8:22-23)

nodes.d: A grievous murrain kills the Egyptians' cattle while none of Israel's die, then ashes sprinkled by Moses become boils on man and beast, even on the magicians. The LORD hardens Pharaoh's heart.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the fifth and sixth plagues and what was different for Israel?
ev: Say what happened to the livestock of Egypt and of Israel (9:6)
Say what happened to the magicians (9:11)

nodes.d: God tells Pharaoh he has raised him up to show his power and make his name known in all the earth, and sends hail with fire that destroys everything in the fields, except in Goshen. Pharaoh says he has sinned and the LORD is righteous, but hardens his heart again when the hail stops.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Pharaoh said after the hail and what he did once it stopped?
ev: Say why God said he had raised Pharaoh up (9:16)
Say what some servants did when they feared the word of the LORD (9:20)
Describe Pharaoh's confession and what followed (9:27-35)

nodes.d: God says he has hardened Pharaoh so that parents may tell their children of the signs. His servants urge him to let the men go, but Pharaoh will not release the families; locusts cover Egypt and eat what the hail left, and after Pharaoh's confession the LORD removes them but hardens his heart.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Moses wanted to take with him to the feast in 10:9 and what the locusts did?
ev: Say why the LORD said he did these signs (10:2)
Say what Pharaoh offered and what Moses asked for (10:8-11)

nodes.d: Thick darkness covers Egypt for three days while Israel has light in their dwellings. Pharaoh offers to let the people go but keep their flocks, Moses refuses, and Pharaoh tells Moses never to see his face again.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the ninth plague and where there was light?
ev: Say how long the darkness lasted and where there was light (10:22-23)
Say why Moses insisted on taking the livestock (10:25-26)

nodes.d: God tells Moses one more plague will bring Pharaoh to let Israel go. Moses announces that at midnight every firstborn in Egypt will die, but not even a dog will move its tongue against Israel, to show that the LORD makes a difference between Egypt and Israel.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what the last plague was to be and how Israel would be treated differently?
ev: Say what Moses announced (11:4-5)
Say how Israel would be treated differently (11:7)

nodes.d: God tells Israel to take an unblemished lamb for each household on the tenth day, kill it at evening on the fourteenth, put its blood on the door posts and lintel, and eat it roasted in haste with unleavened bread and bitter herbs. When he sees the blood he will pass over; the day is to be kept as a memorial, and children are to be told what it means.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the Israelites did with the lamb and its blood, and what God promised?
ev: List what the lamb must be like and what was done with its blood (12:5-7)
Say what God promised when he saw the blood (12:13)
Say what parents were to tell their children (12:26-27)

nodes.t: The firstborn die and Israel leaves Egypt
nodes.d: At midnight the LORD strikes all the firstborn in Egypt, and Pharaoh urges Israel to leave. They go with their dough unleavened, taking silver, gold and clothing given by the Egyptians, about six hundred thousand men on foot, at the end of the four hundred and thirty years.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened at midnight and how Israel left Egypt?
ev: Describe what happened at midnight (12:29-30)
Say what the Egyptians gave Israel (12:35-36)
Say how long the sojourning in Egypt was (12:40-41)

nodes.d: The ordinance of the Passover is set out: no foreigner or hired servant may eat of it, a bought servant who is circumcised may, the lamb is eaten in one house and no bone of it broken, and a sojourner who wants to keep it must be circumcised. One law covers native and stranger.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what the Passover rules say about foreigners and about the lamb's bones?
ev: Say what is required of a stranger who wants to keep the Passover (12:48)
Say what was not to be done with the lamb's bones (12:46)

nodes.t: The firstborn and the feast of unleavened bread
nodes.d: God says all the firstborn of man and beast are his; the firstborn of men are to be redeemed and an ass's firstling redeemed with a lamb. Israel is to remember the day of the exodus, keep the feast of unleavened bread and tell their sons what the LORD did.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say why the firstborn belonged to the LORD and what children were to be told?
ev: Say what God claimed as his in 13:2
Say what Israelites were to tell their sons (13:8, 13:14-15)

nodes.t: Led by the pillar of cloud and fire
nodes.d: God leads Israel by the wilderness way and not the near road through Philistia, lest they see war and return. Moses carries the bones of Joseph, and the LORD goes before them in a pillar of cloud by day and a pillar of fire by night.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how God led Israel out of Egypt, day and night?
ev: Say why God did not lead them by the nearest road (13:17)
Describe how the LORD led them by day and by night (13:21-22)

nodes.d: Pharaoh pursues Israel with chariots and traps them at the sea. Moses says to stand still and see the LORD's salvation; the LORD divides the sea, Israel walks through on dry ground, and the returning waters cover Pharaoh's army.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the crossing of the sea and what Moses told the people to do?
ev: Say what the people said when they saw the Egyptians (14:10-12)
Say what Moses answered (14:13-14)
Say what happened to the Egyptians and how Israel responded (14:27-31)

nodes.t: The song of Moses and Miriam
nodes.d: Moses and Israel sing to the LORD for triumphing over Pharaoh's horse and rider, praising him as strength, song, salvation and warrior, asking who is like him among the gods, and looking ahead to leading his people in to his sanctuary. Miriam leads the women in the refrain.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Israel praised the LORD for in the song at the sea?
ev: Say what the song says the LORD did (15:1, 15:4)
Find where the song says who is like the LORD (15:11)
Say who led the women (15:20-21)

nodes.d: After three days without water Israel comes to Marah, where the water is bitter and the people murmur. The LORD shows Moses a tree which sweetens it, and promises healing for obedience, then they come to Elim.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened at Marah?
ev: Say why the people murmured at Marah (15:23-24)
Say how the water was made sweet (15:25)

nodes.t: Bread from heaven: manna and quails
nodes.d: Israel murmurs for the food of Egypt. The LORD sends quails in the evening and manna in the morning, a day's portion to be gathered daily, with a double portion on the sixth day for the sabbath. An omer of manna is kept before the Testimony.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how the manna was gathered each day and what was different on the sixth and seventh days?
ev: Say what the people were to do each day and on the sixth day (16:4-5, 16:22-26)
Say what happened to manna kept overnight against the command (16:19-20)
Say how long Israel ate manna (16:35)

nodes.d: Exodus follows the sabbath from the manna (16) through the fourth commandment (20:8-11), the law for rest (23:12), and its description as a sign and perpetual covenant (31:12-17) to a final reminder before building the tabernacle (35:1-3).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} trace what Exodus says about the sabbath from the manna to chapter 31?
ev: Say what the fourth commandment says is the reason for the sabbath (20:11)
Say what 31:13 says the sabbath is a sign of

nodes.t: Water from the rock at Massah and Meribah
nodes.d: At Rephidim there is no water, and the people chide Moses and test the LORD. At the LORD's direction Moses strikes the rock at Horeb and water comes out; the place is named Massah and Meribah.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what the people said at Rephidim and how God provided water?
ev: Say what the people asked (17:7)
Say what Moses did and what came of it (17:5-6)

nodes.t: Amalek attacked, and Moses' hands held up
nodes.d: Amalek fights Israel at Rephidim. While Joshua fights, Moses stands on the hill with the rod of God; Israel prevails when his hand is up, and Aaron and Hur support his hands until the sun sets. The LORD says he will blot out Amalek's remembrance.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the battle with Amalek and how Moses' hands were held up?
ev: Say what happened when Moses held up his hand and when he let it down (17:11)
Say who helped Moses (17:12)

nodes.d: Jethro brings Moses' wife and two sons to the mount of God. Moses tells him what the LORD did to Pharaoh and Egypt, and Jethro rejoices, blesses the LORD, says he knows the LORD is greater than all gods, and offers a burnt offering and sacrifices.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Jethro said after hearing what the LORD had done for Israel?
ev: Say what Jethro concluded about the LORD (18:10-11)
Say who ate with Jethro before God (18:12)

nodes.d: Moses sits all day judging the people. Jethro tells him the burden is too heavy and advises him to teach the statutes and appoint able men who fear God as rulers of thousands, hundreds, fifties and tens, bringing only hard cases to him. Moses does so.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Moses appointed other judges and what kind of men he chose?
ev: Say what problem Jethro saw (18:14-18)
Describe the kind of men Moses was to choose (18:21)

nodes.t: At Sinai: a kingdom of priests
nodes.d: In the third month Israel reaches Sinai. God reminds them how he bore them on eagles' wings and says that if they obey his voice and keep his covenant they will be his peculiar treasure, a kingdom of priests and a holy nation. The people answer together that they will do all the LORD has spoken.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what God offered Israel at Sinai in 19:5-6 and how the people answered?
ev: Say what God reminded Israel of (19:4)
Say what God said Israel would be if they obeyed and kept his covenant (19:5-6)
Say how the people answered (19:8)

nodes.t: The LORD descends on Mount Sinai
nodes.d: Israel is told to sanctify themselves and not to touch the mountain. On the third day there are thunders, lightning, a thick cloud and a loud trumpet, and the LORD descends on Sinai in fire; Moses goes up and is told to warn the people again.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what happened when the LORD came down on Mount Sinai, and why bounds were set?
ev: Say how the people prepared (19:10-15)
Describe what happened on the third day (19:16-19)
Say what boundary was set and why (19:12, 19:21)

nodes.d: God speaks all these words, beginning by saying he is the LORD who brought Israel out of Egypt. They cover having no other gods, no images, not taking his name in vain, remembering the sabbath, honouring father and mother, and not killing, committing adultery, stealing, bearing false witness or coveting.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say the Ten Commandments in order and say what comes before them in 20:2?
ev: Recite the ten commandments in order from the Bible
Say what 20:2 says before the commandments begin
Say the reason given for the sabbath (20:11)

nodes.t: The people stand afar off; altars of earth
nodes.d: The people see the thunder, lightning and smoke, tremble, and ask Moses to speak with them rather than God lest they die. Moses says God has come to prove them so that they sin not, and God then gives instructions about no gods of silver or gold and about altars of earth or uncut stone.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say why the people stood far off and what they asked Moses to do?
ev: Say what the people asked Moses (20:19)
Say what Moses said was God's purpose (20:20)

nodes.d: God sets judgments before Israel, beginning with Hebrew servants: a servant serves six years and goes out free in the seventh, and rules protect a servant's wife and a maidservant sold by her father.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what the law of 21:2 said about a Hebrew servant?
ev: Say what must happen in the seventh year (21:2)
Say what protections 21:7-11 gives a woman

nodes.d: Laws deal with striking and killing, a refuge for accidental killing, striking or cursing parents, kidnapping, injuries, the life-for-life principle and an owner's responsibility for a goring ox or an open pit.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the difference between the cases in 21:12-14?
ev: Say how deliberate and accidental killing are treated differently (21:12-14)
Find the verses that state life for life, eye for eye (21:23-25)

nodes.d: Laws require restitution for stolen and damaged property, such as five oxen for an ox, and set rules for animals that trespass, fire, goods left in trust and borrowed animals.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what the law required of a thief in 22:1-4?
ev: Say what a thief had to give back (22:1, 22:4)
Say what was required when a man's beast fed in another's field (22:5)

nodes.t: Judgments: purity, the poor and the stranger
nodes.d: Laws cover seduction of a maid, sorcery, sacrificing to another god, and care for strangers, widows, the fatherless and the poor, whom Israel must not oppress because they themselves were strangers in Egypt. Firstfruits and the firstborn are to be given to the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what 22:21-27 says about strangers, widows and the poor and why?
ev: Say how strangers, widows and orphans were to be treated and why (22:21-24)
Say what was to be done with a neighbour's pledged cloak (22:26-27)

nodes.d: Israel is not to spread false reports, follow a crowd to pervert justice, favour the poor or wrest justice from the poor, take a bribe or oppress a stranger; they must even return an enemy's straying ox and help his fallen ass.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what 23:1-9 teaches about honesty in court and fairness?
ev: List some commands about witnesses and judgment (23:1-3, 23:6-8)
Say what to do if you see your enemy's ox going astray (23:4-5)

nodes.t: Judgments: sabbath years and three feasts
nodes.d: The land is to rest in the seventh year so the poor may eat, and every seventh day all work is to rest. Three times a year Israel keeps a feast: unleavened bread, harvest and ingathering.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name the three yearly feasts and the rest of the seventh day and seventh year?
ev: Say why the land was to rest in the seventh year (23:11)
Name the three feasts (23:14-16)

nodes.t: The angel before Israel and the land
nodes.d: God promises to send an Angel before Israel to bring them to the prepared place, saying his name is in him. If they obey, he will be an enemy to their enemies and drive out the nations little by little; they must not serve those nations' gods or make a covenant with them.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what God promised about the Angel and the land, and what Israel was not to do?
ev: Say what God promised and what he required (23:20-25)
Say why the nations would be driven out gradually (23:29-30)

nodes.d: Moses tells the people all the LORD's words and judgments, and they answer with one voice that they will do them. Moses writes the words, builds an altar and twelve pillars, reads the book of the covenant, and sprinkles the people with blood, saying it is the blood of the covenant the LORD has made with them.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what happened when the covenant was made in Exodus 24, and what Moses said as he sprinkled the blood?
ev: Say how the people answered (24:3, 24:7)
Say what Moses did with the blood and what he said (24:6-8)

nodes.t: The elders see God; Moses on the mountain
nodes.d: Moses, Aaron, Nadab, Abihu and seventy elders go up and see the God of Israel and eat and drink. Moses goes further up with Joshua into the cloud, where the glory of the LORD abides on Sinai and he stays forty days and forty nights.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say who went up the mountain in Exodus 24 and how long Moses stayed?
ev: Say who went up and what they saw and did (24:9-11)
Say how long Moses stayed on the mountain and what covered it (24:15-18)

nodes.d: God tells Moses to ask Israel for a willing offering of gold, silver, brass, fabrics, skins, wood, oil, spices and stones, so they can make a sanctuary so that he may dwell among them, according to the pattern he shows.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say why God asked for a sanctuary and how the gifts were to be given?
ev: Say how the offering was to be given (25:2)
Say why God wanted the sanctuary (25:8)

nodes.d: From the command to build a sanctuary so God may dwell among Israel (25:8) through his promise to meet them and be their God (29:43-46), Moses' plea that his presence go with them (33:14-15), to the glory filling the tabernacle (40:34-35).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} trace how Exodus moves from "let them make me a sanctuary" to the glory filling it?
ev: Say what God said in 25:8 and 29:45-46
Say how the book ends (40:34-35)

nodes.t: The ark and the mercy seat
nodes.d: Moses is told to make an ark of acacia wood overlaid with gold, to put the testimony in it, and to make a gold mercy seat with two cherubim on top, where God says he will meet and speak with Moses.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the ark and say what God said would happen above the mercy seat?
ev: Say what was to be put in the ark (25:16)
Say what God said would happen at the mercy seat (25:22)

nodes.t: The table and the golden lampstand
nodes.d: Instructions are given for a gold-covered table for the bread of the presence and a pure gold lampstand with seven lamps, made after the pattern shown on the mount.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name the two furnishings made in 25:23-40?
ev: Say what was to be set on the table (25:30)
Say how many lamps the lampstand had (25:37)

nodes.d: The tabernacle is to be made of ten linen curtains with cherubim, goat-hair curtains and skin coverings, upright boards in silver sockets, and a veil that divides the holy place from the most holy place, where the ark is to be set.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what the veil in 26:31-33 was for?
ev: Say what the veil separated (26:33)
Say what was to go in the most holy place (26:33-34)

nodes.t: The bronze altar and the court
nodes.d: Instructions for an altar of acacia wood overlaid with bronze, a court enclosed by linen hangings on bronze pillars, and pure olive oil so a lamp burns always before the veil, tended by Aaron and his sons.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what stood in the court of the tabernacle according to 27:1-19?
ev: Say what the altar of 27:1-8 was made of
Say who was to tend the lamp (27:21)

nodes.t: Aaron and his sons: the priestly garments
nodes.d: Aaron and his sons are to be priests, with holy garments for glory and beauty: ephod, breastplate with twelve stones for the tribes, robe with bells, a turban with a gold plate "Holiness to the LORD", and linen undergarments. Aaron bears the names of Israel on his shoulders and heart.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Aaron carried on his shoulders and heart when he went in before the LORD?
ev: Say what names were on the stones of the ephod and breastplate (28:9-12, 28:21)
Say what was engraved on the gold plate (28:36)

nodes.d: Aaron and his sons are washed, clothed, anointed and consecrated over seven days with a bullock and rams. Daily lambs are offered at morning and evening, and God says he will meet Israel there, sanctify the tabernacle and dwell among them.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what was done to make Aaron and his sons priests and what God promised in 29:45-46?
ev: Name some steps of the consecration (29:4-9, 29:20-21)
Say what God promised in 29:45-46

nodes.t: The incense altar and the atonement money
nodes.d: God gives instructions for a gold altar of incense before the veil, burned morning and evening, with atonement made on its horns once a year, and for a half-shekel ransom for each person numbered, rich and poor alike.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what the atonement money was and who gave it?
ev: Say what was to be burned on the altar and when (30:7-8)
Say how much each person gave (30:13-15)

nodes.t: The laver, anointing oil and incense
nodes.d: A bronze laver is made for priests to wash hands and feet before entering the tabernacle or approaching the altar, lest they die. A holy anointing oil and a special incense are described; neither may be copied for ordinary use.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what the laver was for and why Aaron and his sons washed?
ev: Say when Aaron and his sons were to wash (30:19-21)
Say what was forbidden about the anointing oil and incense (30:32-33, 30:37-38)

nodes.d: The LORD calls by name Bezalel of the tribe of Judah and fills him with the spirit of God in wisdom and workmanship, and gives Aholiab of Dan and others to help make the tabernacle and all its furnishings.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say who God appointed to build the tabernacle and what equipped him?
ev: Say who was called and what filled him (31:2-3)
Say what he was to make (31:7-11)

nodes.t: The sabbath as a sign; the tablets of testimony
nodes.d: God says Israel must keep his sabbaths as a sign between him and them throughout their generations, a perpetual covenant, grounded in his six days of making and rest on the seventh. At the end he gives Moses two tablets of stone written by the finger of God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say why the sabbath is called a sign and what God gave Moses on the mountain?
ev: Say what the sabbath is called in 31:13, 31:16-17
Say what God gave Moses at the end of the conversation (31:18)

nodes.d: When Moses delays on the mountain, the people ask Aaron to make gods for them. Aaron collects their gold earrings and fashions a molten calf, builds an altar and proclaims a feast, and the people offer sacrifices and rise up to play.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what the people did while Moses was on the mountain?
ev: Say what the people asked and what Aaron made (32:1-4)
Say what Aaron proclaimed (32:5)

nodes.d: God tells Moses the people have corrupted themselves and he will consume them and make a great nation of Moses. Moses pleads that the LORD brought them out and remember Abraham, Isaac and Israel, and the LORD repents of the evil he thought to do.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say how Moses pleaded for Israel and what he asked God to remember?
ev: Say what God threatened (32:9-10)
Say what Moses asked God to remember (32:13)
Say what the LORD did in response (32:14)

nodes.t: Moses breaks the tablets; judgment on the calf
nodes.d: Moses comes down with tablets written by God, sees the calf, breaks the tablets, burns the calf and makes Israel drink it. The Levites answer his call to be on the LORD's side, about three thousand fall, and Moses goes back to seek atonement and offers to be blotted out with them; the LORD plagues the people.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Moses did when he saw the calf and what he asked God in 32:32?
ev: Say what Moses did with the tablets and the calf (32:19-20)
Say what Aaron said in his defence (32:22-24)
Say what Moses asked the LORD in 32:32

nodes.t: The tent of meeting and the cloud
nodes.d: God tells Israel to go to the land but says he will not go up in their midst because they are stiffnecked, and the people mourn. Moses pitches a tent outside the camp where the cloudy pillar descends and the LORD speaks with him face to face as with a friend.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say why Moses pitched the tent outside the camp and how the LORD spoke with him there?
ev: Say what God said he would not do (33:3)
Describe how the LORD spoke with Moses (33:9-11)

nodes.t: Moses asks to see God's glory
nodes.d: Moses asks that God's presence go with them and then to see his glory. The LORD says his presence will go with Moses, that he will make all his goodness pass and proclaim his name, but no man can see his face and live; Moses is hidden in a cleft of the rock and sees only his back.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Moses asked to see and how God answered?
ev: Say what Moses asked in 33:15 and 33:18
Say what God said he would do and what he would not allow (33:19-23)

nodes.d: Moses hews two new tablets and goes up Sinai, where the LORD descends in the cloud and proclaims his name as merciful, gracious, longsuffering and abundant in goodness and truth, forgiving iniquity yet not clearing the guilty. Moses bows and asks God to go among them and pardon their sin.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say how the LORD described himself in 34:6-7 and what Moses asked?
ev: List words from 34:6-7 that describe the LORD
Say what Moses asked in 34:9

nodes.t: The covenant renewed and the words written
nodes.d: The LORD says he makes a covenant and will do marvels, and commands Israel to destroy the altars of the nations, make no covenant with them, make no molten gods, and keep the feasts and the sabbath. He tells Moses to write the words, and after forty days Moses writes on the tables the words of the covenant, the ten commandments.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what the LORD told Moses to write in 34:27-28 and what it is called?
ev: Say what God said in 34:10 and 34:27
Say what was written on the tables (34:28)

nodes.d: Moses comes down with the two tablets and does not know that the skin of his face shines; Aaron and Israel are afraid to come near. Moses speaks to them and wears a veil over his face except when he goes in before the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what happened to Moses' face and when he wore a veil?
ev: Say why people were afraid to come near (34:30)
Say when Moses took the veil off (34:34)

nodes.d: Moses gathers Israel, repeats the sabbath, and calls for the offerings and for every wise-hearted person to make what the LORD commanded. Men and women bring jewels, materials and spun thread with willing hearts.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say how the people responded when Moses asked for offerings for the tabernacle?
ev: Say who brought offerings (35:21-29)
Say what Moses repeated about the sabbath (35:2-3)

nodes.t: Bezalel and the workers build; enough and too much
nodes.d: Moses announces that the LORD has called Bezalel and Aholiab, and the workers receive the offerings. The people bring so much that Moses has the camp stop giving, and the workers make the curtains, boards, bars and veil.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say why Moses told the people to stop bringing offerings?
ev: Say what happened when the people brought too much (36:5-7)
Name what the workers made in chapter 36

nodes.t: The ark, table, lampstand and incense altar are made
nodes.d: Bezalel makes the ark with its mercy seat and cherubim, the table, the lampstand, the incense altar, the anointing oil and the incense, as commanded.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list the furnishings Bezalel made in chapter 37?
ev: Name the furnishings made in chapter 37

nodes.t: The altar, the laver, the court and the accounts
nodes.d: Bezalel makes the altar of burnt offering, the laver from the women's mirrors, and the court, and the metals given for the work are totalled.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Bezalel made in chapter 38 and what the laver was made from?
ev: Say what the laver was made from (38:8)
Say what was counted in 38:24-31

nodes.d: The workers make the holy garments for Aaron: the ephod, the breastplate with its twelve stones, the robe with golden bells, the coats, the turban and the gold plate of "Holiness to the LORD", as the LORD commanded Moses.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name some of the garments made for Aaron in chapter 39?
ev: Name pieces of Aaron's clothing made in chapter 39
Say what phrase "as the LORD commanded Moses" shows about how the work was done

nodes.t: The work is finished and Moses blesses Israel
nodes.d: All the parts of the tabernacle are brought to Moses, who inspects them, sees they were made as the LORD commanded, and blesses the people.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Moses did when he saw the finished work?
ev: Say what Moses did when he saw the finished work (39:43)

nodes.d: On the first day of the first month in the second year Moses sets up the tabernacle, puts the testimony in the ark, arranges the table, lampstand, altars and laver, hangs the court, anoints and washes, as the LORD commanded.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say when the tabernacle was set up and what Moses put into the ark?
ev: Say when the tabernacle was set up (40:2, 40:17)
Say what Moses put in the ark (40:20)

nodes.t: The glory of the LORD fills the tabernacle
nodes.d: A cloud covers the tent and the glory of the LORD fills the tabernacle so that Moses cannot enter. Israel travels only when the cloud lifts, and the cloud is on the tabernacle by day and fire by night in the sight of all Israel.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what happened when the tabernacle was finished and how Israel knew when to move?
ev: Say what filled the tabernacle (40:34)
Say how Israel knew when to travel (40:36-37)

nodes.d: Genesis runs from creation (1:1) to the death of Joseph in Egypt (50:26): creation, the fall, the flood, Babel, and the patriarchs Abraham, Isaac, Jacob and Joseph.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline Genesis in order, from creation to Joseph in Egypt?
ev: Name the four main sections: creation, fall and flood, Abraham, and the patriarchs through Joseph
Say where the story begins (1:1) and ends (50:26)

nodes.d: God creates the heavens and the earth, and all that fills them, in six days, and rests on the seventh.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what God made on each day, and what happened on the seventh?
ev: Retell what God made on each of the six days
Say that God rested on the seventh day and blessed it

nodes.d: God confirms his promise of offspring and land to Abram and makes a covenant with him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what God promised Abram in Genesis 15 and how Abram responded?
ev: Describe the promises of offspring and land
Read 15:6 and say what Abram believed

nodes.d: God appears to Abram at ninety-nine, changes his name to Abraham, and gives circumcision as the sign of the covenant.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what circumcision was a sign of in Genesis 17?
ev: Explain the name change (17:5)
State what circumcision signified (17:10-11)

nodes.t: Joseph is raised up in Egypt
nodes.d: Joseph interprets Pharaoh's dreams and is set over the land of Egypt.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Joseph came to rule in Egypt?
ev: Retell the dreams and what Joseph advised

nodes.t: God meant it for good: providence
nodes.d: Joseph tells his brothers that although they meant evil, God meant it for good (50:20); Paul teaches a similar confidence in Romans 8:28.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Joseph meant in Genesis 50:20?
ev: Explain Genesis 50:20 in context
Compare it with Romans 8:28

nodes.d: Jacob blesses his sons, and says the sceptre shall not depart from Judah.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Jacob promised Judah in Genesis 49:10?
ev: Read 49:10 and identify to whom the blessing is addressed

nodes.d: The gospel of Matthew, from the genealogy of Jesus Christ, son of David and son of Abraham (1:1), through the five great discourses, the passion and the resurrection, to the closing commission (28:16-20).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain in a few sentences what Matthew is about and how it begins and ends?
ev: Describe the movement of the book: birth and preparation (1-4), the Sermon on the Mount (5-7), miracles and mission (8-12), parables of the kingdom (13), teaching on the way to Jerusalem (14-23), the coming kingdom (24-25), the passion and resurrection (26-28)
Name where the book starts and ends

nodes.d: Jesus takes the commandments against killing and adultery to the heart: anger and contempt, and lustful looks, are judged, and reconciliation and cutting off sin are urged.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Jesus deepens the commands about murder and adultery?
ev: Contrast “ye have heard” with “I say unto you” in 5:21-22 and 27-28
Describe what Jesus says to do before offering a gift at the altar

nodes.t: Divorce, oaths, retaliation and love for enemies
nodes.d: Jesus teaches on divorce, on plain speech instead of oaths, on not resisting evil with evil, and on loving and praying for enemies, as the Father gives sun and rain to evil and good.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus says about loving enemies and why?
ev: Say what Jesus teaches about oaths (5:33-37)
Explain the command about enemies and the reason given in 5:45

nodes.d: Pharisees accuse the disciples of breaking the tradition of the elders; Jesus charges them with voiding God’s commandment by tradition and says what comes out of the heart, not what goes into the mouth, defiles.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus said defiles a person?
ev: Give Jesus’ example of tradition overriding a commandment
List what comes out of the heart (15:19)

nodes.t: The rich young man and rewards of following
nodes.d: A young man asks what good thing earns eternal life; told to keep the commandments and then to sell all and follow, he goes away sorrowful; Jesus speaks of the camel and needle and promises rewards to those who left all.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Jesus asked the young man to do and why it was hard?
ev: Say why the young man left sorrowful
Explain “with God all things are possible”

nodes.d: Sadducees pose a puzzle about a woman married to seven brothers; Jesus says they err not knowing the scriptures or God’s power, that in the resurrection they are as angels, and that God is God of the living.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain Jesus’ answer about the resurrection?
ev: Say what the Sadducees denied
Explain how Jesus uses the words about Abraham, Isaac and Jacob

nodes.d: The gospel of Mark, from “the beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God” (1:1) through Jesus’ ministry in Galilee, the road to Jerusalem and his death, to the empty tomb and commission.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain in a few sentences what Mark is about and where it begins and ends?
ev: Describe the movement of the book: John and the start of ministry (1), Galilee (1-8), the way to Jerusalem (8-10), the last week and passion (11-15), the empty tomb (16)
Say what Mark calls the book in 1:1

nodes.t: Tradition of the elders and what defiles
nodes.d: Pharisees fault the disciples for eating with unwashed hands; Jesus quotes Isaiah on lip service, charges them with setting aside God’s commandment through Corban, and says what comes out of the heart defiles.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus says defiles a person?
ev: Explain Jesus’ Corban example
List what proceeds from the heart (7:21-22)

nodes.t: The rich man who went away sorrowful
nodes.d: A man runs to ask what he must do to inherit eternal life; Jesus loves him and tells him to sell all and follow, and he leaves sad; Jesus teaches about the difficulty of riches and what God can do and promises to those who leave all.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Jesus asked of the rich man and why he left sad?
ev: Say what Jesus lists and then asks of the man
Explain “with God all things are possible”

nodes.d: Sadducees who deny the resurrection ask about a woman married to seven brothers; Jesus says they err not knowing the scriptures or God’s power, that the risen are as angels, and that God is God of the living, citing the bush.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain Jesus’ answer about the resurrection?
ev: Say what the Sadducees asked
Explain Jesus’ use of the words from the bush

nodes.t: Simeon and Anna in the Temple
nodes.d: Jesus is named and presented at the temple; Simeon, to whom the Spirit promised he would see the Lord's Christ, blesses God for salvation for all peoples, and Anna the prophetess speaks of him to those awaiting redemption.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Simeon and Anna said when they saw the child Jesus?
ev: Say what Simeon was waiting for and what he and Anna said.

nodes.d: A ruler asks what to do to inherit eternal life, says he has kept the commandments, and is told to sell all and follow; he goes away sorrowful, and Jesus says it is hard for the rich to enter the kingdom but possible with God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the story of the rich ruler and Jesus' words about what is impossible and possible?
ev: Retell what the ruler asked, what Jesus told him and what Jesus said is possible with God.

nodes.t: The Sadducees Ask About the Resurrection
nodes.d: The Sadducees, who deny the resurrection, ask whose wife a woman married to seven brothers would be; Jesus says those counted worthy of that world neither marry nor die, and the dead are raised, as Moses called the Lord the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain Jesus' answer to the Sadducees about the resurrection?
ev: Say what Jesus said about the resurrection and how he used Moses.

nodes.t: I Am the Bread of Life
nodes.d: The crowd seeks Jesus for the loaves; he says to labour for food that endures, that believing is the work of God, that Moses did not give the true bread from heaven, and that he is the bread of life; all the Father gives him will come and he will raise them at the last day.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus means by 'I am the bread of life' in this passage?
ev: Say what Jesus says he is and what he promises those who come to him.

nodes.t: His Side Pierced and the Burial
nodes.d: The soldiers do not break Jesus' legs but pierce his side, and John says these things fulfil Scripture; Joseph of Arimathaea and Nicodemus wrap his body with spices and lay it in a new tomb in a garden.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what happened to Jesus' body after his death and who buried him?
ev: Say what the soldiers did and who buried Jesus.

nodes.d: Acts continues Luke's account from the ascension of Jesus (1:9) to Paul preaching at Rome (28:31): the Holy Ghost at Pentecost, the church in Jerusalem, the witness spreading to Judaea, Samaria and the Gentiles, and Paul's journeys, arrest and voyage to Rome.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline how the gospel spreads in Acts from Jerusalem to Rome?
ev: Say how Acts 1:8 gives the shape of the book (Jerusalem, Judaea, Samaria, the uttermost part)
Name the major sections: Peter in Jerusalem, Stephen and Philip, Saul's conversion, Cornelius, Paul's journeys, Paul's arrest and Rome

nodes.d: Peter tells the amazed crowd that the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob glorified his Son Jesus, whom they delivered up, and that faith in his name made the man strong. He calls them to repent so that their sins may be blotted out, and reminds them of God's covenant with the fathers and the blessing promised to Abraham's seed.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Peter said made the man walk and what he urged the crowd to do?
ev: Say whom Peter credits for the healing (3:12-16)
Explain what Peter calls the people to do and why (3:18-19, 3:25-26)

nodes.t: Stephen's speech: Moses and the people's refusal
nodes.d: Stephen recounts Israel's growth in Egypt, the birth and upbringing of Moses, his first attempt to help his brethren and their rejection, and God's call from the burning bush. He says the people refused Moses, turned back in their hearts to Egypt, and made a calf.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Stephen says Israel treated Moses, whom God sent as ruler and deliverer?
ev: Retell the stages of Moses' life Stephen names (7:20-36)
Say how Stephen says the fathers treated Moses (7:35, 7:39-41)

nodes.t: Paul before the council: the resurrection
nodes.d: Paul tells the council he has lived in all good conscience, and when the high priest orders him struck, he rebukes him and then says he did not know he was the high priest. Perceiving Sadducees and Pharisees, he says he is called in question for the hope of the resurrection, the council divides, and the Lord stands by him that night to say he must bear witness at Rome.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Paul used the question of the resurrection before the council?
ev: Say how Paul divided the council (23:6-9)
State what the Lord told Paul that night (23:11)

nodes.d: Paul answers the question of Israel by pointing to God's sovereign choice, from Isaac and Jacob onward, and his mercy.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Romans 9 says about God's choice and mercy?
ev: Link 9:7 to Genesis 21:12 and 9:12 to Genesis 25:23
Explain 9:15-16

nodes.d: Paul writes to the church at Corinth about divisions, sin in the church, questions they asked him, worship, the resurrection and the collection (1:1-16:24).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} give a short outline of 1 Corinthians and name three problems Paul corrects in the Corinthian church?
ev: Name the main problems Paul addresses: divisions, immorality, lawsuits, marriage, food offered to idols, the Lord's supper, gifts, the resurrection
Say who the letter is addressed to from 1:2

nodes.t: Warnings from Israel in the wilderness
nodes.d: Paul reminds the Corinthians that Israel passed through the sea and ate and drank spiritual food, yet many fell; he says these things were examples to us, and that God provides a way of escape from temptation.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul uses Israel's failures as a warning, and what God promises in 1 Corinthians 10:13?
ev: List the privileges of Israel in 10:1-4 and the sins in 10:7-10
Explain why Paul says these things were written (10:11)
State the promise of 10:13

nodes.d: Paul's second letter to the Corinthians: comfort in affliction, the ministry of the new covenant and reconciliation, the collection for the saints, and a defence of his apostleship (1:1-13:14).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} give a short outline of 2 Corinthians and say what its three main parts are about?
ev: Name the main sections: comfort and ministry (1-7), the collection (8-9), Paul's defence of his apostleship (10-13)
Say what Paul tells the Corinthians about his sufferings

nodes.d: Paul blesses God as the Father of mercies, who comforts us in trouble so that we can comfort others, and tells of a deadly trouble in Asia that taught him to trust in God who raises the dead.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why God comforts us, using 2 Corinthians 1:3-4?
ev: Say who God is called in 1:3
Explain why we are comforted (1:4)
Explain what Paul learned from the trouble in Asia (1:8-10)

nodes.t: All God's promises are yes in Christ
nodes.d: Paul defends changing his travel plans, saying his word is not yes and no, because God is true and in Christ all the promises of God are yes; God has established, anointed and sealed believers and given the Spirit as a guarantee.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what it means that all the promises of God are yes in Christ (2 Corinthians 1:20)?
ev: Explain what Paul says about God's promises in 1:20
List what God has done for believers in 1:21-22
Say why Paul had not yet come to Corinth (1:23)

nodes.t: Unveiled face: from glory to glory
nodes.d: Paul says Moses put a veil over his face, a veil that remains in the reading of the old testament but is done away in Christ, and that believers with open face behold the glory of the Lord and are changed into his image.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what happens to a person who turns to the Lord, using 2 Corinthians 3:16-18?
ev: Explain the veil of Moses (3:13-15)
Say when the veil is taken away (3:16)
Explain what happens to those who behold the Lord's glory (3:18)

nodes.d: Paul's letter to the saints at Ephesus: God's blessings in Christ, salvation by grace, the unity of Jew and Gentile in one body, and how to walk worthy in the church, home and spiritual battle (1:1-6:24).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} give a short outline of Ephesians and say what its two halves are about?
ev: Describe the two halves: what God has done in Christ (1-3) and how to walk worthy (4-6)

nodes.d: Paul tells children to obey their parents in the Lord, quotes the commandment to honour father and mother, tells fathers to bring children up in the Lord, and gives instructions to servants and masters who both answer to a Master in heaven.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Paul tells children and parents in Ephesians 6:1-4?
ev: Quote the commandment Paul cites (6:2)
Say what fathers are told (6:4)
Say what masters are reminded of (6:9)

nodes.t: A better covenant: the new covenant promised
nodes.d: Jesus ministers in the true tabernacle as mediator of a better covenant on better promises; the writer cites the promise of a new covenant, in which God will write his laws on hearts, be their God, and remember their sins no more, making the first old.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what the writer says God promised in the new covenant (8:8-12)?
ev: State what is better about the covenant (8:6)
List the promises of 8:10-12
Say what 8:13 says about the first covenant

nodes.t: Christ's own blood and the mediator of the new testament
nodes.d: Christ entered the heavenly sanctuary once by his own blood, obtained eternal redemption, and is the mediator of the new testament; the first was dedicated with blood, without shedding of blood there is no remission, and he will appear a second time without sin for salvation.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the writer says Christ's blood does what the blood of bulls and goats could not (9:12-14)?
ev: Contrast animal blood and Christ's blood (9:12-14)
State what 9:22 says about blood and remission
Describe the two appearings in 9:26-28

nodes.t: By faith Moses, Israel and Rahab
nodes.d: By faith Moses' parents hid him, Moses chose affliction with God's people over Egypt's pleasures, kept the Passover, Israel crossed the Red Sea and the walls of Jericho fell, and Rahab was not destroyed.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what Moses chose by faith and why (11:24-27)?
ev: List what Moses did by faith (11:24-28)
Name the two events of 11:29-30

nodes.t: Not Mount Sinai but Mount Zion
nodes.d: Believers have not come to the fearful mountain of Sinai but to mount Zion, the heavenly Jerusalem, to God, to Jesus the mediator of the new covenant and to the blood of sprinkling; they must not refuse the one who speaks, and receive a kingdom that cannot be shaken.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Hebrews 12:18-24 contrasts Sinai with Zion and names Jesus there?
ev: Contrast the two mountains (12:18-24)
State what is said of the kingdom and of God (12:28-29)

nodes.d: The letter to the Hebrews presents Jesus as God's Son, greater than angels and Moses, our great high priest after Melchizedek who mediates a better covenant by one sacrifice, and calls readers to faith and endurance.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain in a few sentences what Hebrews teaches about Jesus and what the readers are told to do?
ev: Describe the main parts: the Son (1-2), Moses and rest (3-4), the high priest (4-7), the new covenant and sacrifice (8-10), faith (11), endurance and exhortations (12-13)

nodes.d: James rebukes giving the rich seats of honour and shaming the poor in the assembly, reminds them God chose the poor rich in faith, and calls loving your neighbour the royal law.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what James says is wrong with favouring the rich over the poor?
ev: Describe the example of partiality in the assembly
Say what James calls the royal law
Explain why partiality is sin according to 2:9

nodes.t: The living stone and the holy priesthood
nodes.d: Peter calls Christ the living stone chosen by God, says believers are built up as a spiritual house and royal priesthood, and says they were once not a people but are now the people of God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name three things Peter calls believers in 1 Peter 2:9?
ev: Explain the stone picture in 2:4-8
List the names Peter gives believers in 2:9
Say what 2:10 says changed for them

nodes.d: The seven angels pour out bowls on the earth, sea, rivers, sun, the beast's throne, Euphrates and air, with a call to watch, gathering at Armageddon, a great earthquake and Babylon remembered before God, while people curse God and do not repent.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list the seven bowls and how people respond?
ev: List what each of the seven bowls is poured on
Say what the angel of the waters says about God in 16:5-7
Say how people respond in 16:9, 11 and 21
